entries.description: Checked WHICH JOB failed before claiming the prediction landed. Both runs reported 'failure' at run level — but run 001 also reported failure while its gds job SUCCEEDED (gl_test was the failure). Had I read the run-level status, I would have scored a prediction correct on a signal that means something different.

Scored the prediction as outcome-correct/mechanism-wrong rather than as a win. Predicted 3x2 fails at routing and 2x2 by not fitting; both failed at detailed placement. Also predicted 94.5%/142% utilisation against a measured 85.0%/129.9% — the arithmetic included tile margins the flow excludes.

Ruled the sweep must precede the pipe run on the grounds that it CHANGES WHAT THE PIPE RUN'S BARS ARE — if 3x2 fails, the area prediction becomes a bar rather than a bonus. Running pipe first would pre-register against an unmeasured requirement: the guessed-threshold defect one level up.

findings.description: The design REQUIRES 4x2 (8 tiles). 3x2 and 2x2 both fail the harden; RTL byte-identical across all three points, info.yaml the only difference. Prediction correct on outcome.

MECHANISM WRONG, and sharper than predicted: both smaller shapes failed at [DPL-0036] DETAILED PLACEMENT inside RepairDesignPostGPL — neither reached routing. The binding constraint below 4x2 is placement legalisation after repair-buffer insertion, not routing congestion. Repair buffers do not merely cost area; below a certain die they make the design UNPLACEABLE.

MY SWEEP DESIGN WAS WRONG: failed runs emit no metrics.csv, only GDS_logs, so a failed point contributes NOTHING to the repair-buffer curve. Got one point, not three. The curve needs sweeping UPWARD (6x2, 8x2) where runs succeed — downward answers 'what is the minimum', upward answers 'how does repair cost scale'.
findings.artifact_link: SWEEP_002_RESULT.md — the curve cannot be built downward
